name: MAX44009 ambient light sensor
description: Maxim ambient light sensor with a human-eye spectral response and automatic ranging over 0.045 to 188,000 lux (22-bit dynamic range, reported as a 4-bit exponent and 8-bit mantissa) over I2C. The chip runs on 1.7-3.6 V and its pins are rated to 4 V absolute maximum. Sold as: GY-49 MAX44009 module (purple, 4-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA; two extra unlabelled pads for the address and INT), I2C address 0x4A (0x4B with A0 high).
eli5: Measures how bright the light is, in lux, from moonlight to full sunshine. Give it 3.3 V.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply: use 3.3 V (the MAX44009 itself is rated 1.7-3.6 V)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, up to 400 kHz (needs a pull-up to 3.3 V)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, open-drain (needs a pull-up to 3.3 V)

supplierQuery: GY-49 MAX44009 ambient light sensor module I2C
buildNotes: Header order on the GY-49 is VIN, GND, SCL, SDA. The two unlabelled pads on the other edge are the address (A0) and INT pins.
Power it from 3.3 V: the MAX44009 operates at 1.7-3.6 V and every pin except INT is rated to only 4 V absolute maximum. Do not wire SDA/SCL to 5 V logic.
The datasheet requires pull-up resistors on SDA and SCL (10 kOhm in its application circuit); Sparkbench adds them. Extra pull-ups already on a board are harmless in parallel.
Address 0x4A with A0 low, 0x4B with A0 high. If the board leaves A0 floating the address can wander: tie the A0 pad to GND if readings come and go.
Lux = 2^E x M x 0.045, with E = bits 7..4 of register 0x03 and M = (bits 3..0 of 0x03) << 4 | (bits 3..0 of 0x04). Exponent 15 means overrange.
Read 0x03 and 0x04 with a Repeated START between them (no STOP), as the datasheet's Figure 8 shows, so both halves come from the same conversion.
In the default mode the chip measures once every 800 ms; the first result is ready about 800 ms after power-up.

The simulator reproduces the chip's register bytes for 368.64-734.4 lux, the range in which the automatic ranging uses exponent 6 (2.88 lux per count); the real chip covers 0.045-188,000 lux by changing the exponent itself.

driver.code:
# MAX44009 ambient light sensor (Maxim 19-5719 Rev 0), MicroPython driver.
# 8-bit registers: 0x00 interrupt status, 0x01 interrupt enable, 0x02 configuration
# (CONT bit 7, MANUAL bit 6, CDR bit 3, TIM[2:0]; power-on 0x03), 0x03 lux high byte
# (E3..E0 M7..M4), 0x04 lux low byte (bits 3..0 = M3..M0), 0x05/0x06 upper/lower
# threshold, 0x07 threshold timer.
#   Full resolution:  lux = 2**E * M[7:0] * 0.045
#   High byte only:   lux = 2**E * M[7:4] * 0.72
# Exponent 15 (0b1111) means overrange.
# The datasheet requires a Repeated START (no STOP) between reading 0x03 and 0x04 so
# both bytes come from the same conversion (Figure 8).
import time

_REG_INT_STATUS = 0x00
_REG_INT_ENABLE = 0x01
_REG_CONFIG = 0x02
_REG_LUX_HIGH = 0x03
_REG_LUX_LOW = 0x04
_REG_THRESH_HIGH = 0x05
_REG_THRESH_LOW = 0x06
_REG_THRESH_TIMER = 0x07

_CONT = 0x80    # continuous conversions (otherwise one every 800 ms)
_MANUAL = 0x40  # manual CDR/TIM; 0 = automatic ranging (power-up default)
_CDR = 0x08     # divide the photodiode current by 8 (manual mode)

ADDR_A0_GND = 0x4A
ADDR_A0_VCC = 0x4B

# TIM[2:0] -> integration time in ms (Table 7)
_TIM_MS = (800, 400, 200, 100, 50, 25, 12.5, 6.25)


class MAX44009:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR_A0_GND, continuous=False, manual=None):
        """addr 0x4A (A0 to GND) or 0x4B (A0 to VCC).
        continuous=False: default mode, one measurement every 800 ms (lowest current).
        manual=None keeps automatic ranging; manual=(cdr, tim) with cdr 0/1 and tim 0-7
        sets the current divider and integration time yourself (Table 9)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        cfg = _CONT if continuous else 0
        if manual is not None:
            cdr, tim = manual
            if not (0 <= tim <= 7) or cdr not in (0, 1):
                raise ValueError('manual=(cdr 0/1, tim 0-7)')
            cfg |= _MANUAL | (_CDR if cdr else 0) | tim
        self._write(_REG_CONFIG, cfg)
        # The first result is ready after one measurement cycle (800 ms in default mode).
        time.sleep_ms(820)

    def _write(self, reg, value):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes((reg, value & 0xFF)))

    def _read(self, reg):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes((reg,)), False)
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 1)[0]

    def raw(self):
        """(exponent, mantissa 0-255) from registers 0x03 and 0x04, read with a Repeated
        START between them so the chip does not update the result in between."""
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes((_REG_LUX_HIGH,)), False)
        hi = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 1, False)[0]
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes((_REG_LUX_LOW,)), False)
        lo = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 1)[0]
        return hi >> 4, ((hi & 0x0F) << 4) | (lo & 0x0F)

    def lux(self):
        """Ambient light in lux at full resolution (0.045 lux LSB at the lowest range)."""
        e, m = self.raw()
        if e == 0x0F:
            raise OSError('MAX44009 overrange (exponent 15)')
        return (1 << e) * m * 0.045

    def lux_high_byte(self):
        """Coarser reading from register 0x03 only (0.72 lux LSB at the lowest range)."""
        hi = self._read(_REG_LUX_HIGH)
        e = hi >> 4
        if e == 0x0F:
            raise OSError('MAX44009 overrange (exponent 15)')
        return (1 << e) * (hi & 0x0F) * 0.72

    def config(self):
        """Configuration register; in automatic mode CDR and TIM show the chosen range."""
        return self._read(_REG_CONFIG)

    def integration_ms(self):
        return _TIM_MS[self.config() & 0x07]

    def interrupt_status(self):
        """1 if the light stayed outside the threshold window (reading clears it)."""
        return self._read(_REG_INT_STATUS) & 0x01

    def set_interrupt(self, enable):
        self._write(_REG_INT_ENABLE, 1 if enable else 0)

    def set_thresholds(self, upper_byte, lower_byte, timer_100ms=0):
        """Threshold registers in the lux-high-byte format EEEE MMMM (datasheet
        'Threshold Register Data Format'); timer in steps of 100 ms."""
        self._write(_REG_THRESH_HIGH, upper_byte)
        self._write(_REG_THRESH_LOW, lower_byte)
        self._write(_REG_THRESH_TIMER, timer_100ms)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from max44009 import MAX44009

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = MAX44009(i2c)  # 0x4A, automatic ranging, one reading every 800 ms
while True:
    print('Lux=%.2f' % sensor.lux())
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the illuminance set on the slider

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
library.simNote: The simulator slider covers 369–734 lux only: the chip reports light as exponent + mantissa, and the model fixes the exponent. The driver handles the full range on real hardware.
library.caveat: The independent reading could not download the manufacturer PDF; register layout and scale were confirmed from library code and the author's reading, not the PDF.
